title: A Medicaid drug subscription model expanded hepatitis-C treatment and produced measurable health and fiscal outcomes
source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35583, using Louisiana Medicaid, hepatitis-C diagnosis, spending, and health-outcome data
geography: Louisiana Medicaid; Louisiana Hepatitis C Elimination Plan beginning in 2019

observations.period: 2018-2022 treatment and diagnosis outcomes; five-year fiscal projection; paper issued August 2026

denominator.unit: Louisiana Medicaid beneficiaries and people with hepatitis C covered by the subscription model; study-specific denominators vary by outcome

treatment_volume.unit: hepatitis-C antiviral treatment volume relative to comparison trend

new_diagnoses.unit: percent change in new hepatitis-C diagnoses

receipt_and_outcome.value: treatment volume and diagnosis outcomes improved; individual treatment completion, cure, access barriers, and household costs are not fully joined

observations.method: Differences-in-differences comparison of spending and treatment outcomes for beneficiaries with hepatitis C versus beneficiaries with diabetes or HIV, using administrative and health data.
observations.uncertainty: The study estimates program-level effects and fiscal savings using comparison groups and projections. It does not provide a single individual-level treatment pathway, and the abstract does not establish equal reach, cure completion, reinfection, or all implementation costs.
observations.subgroup: Louisiana Medicaid beneficiaries with hepatitis C and comparison beneficiaries with diabetes or HIV; diagnosis, treatment, eligibility, incarceration coverage, and access barriers may differ across groups.
observations.counterinterpretation: Treatment expansion and estimated savings may reflect the subscription contract together with outreach, diagnosis, provider behavior, and other implementation changes. Program-level savings do not imply that every eligible person received treatment or that the model transfers unchanged to another state.

related_sources.claim: Official NBER DOI identifies the working paper.

boundary: This record measures a Louisiana Medicaid subscription model through treatment, diagnosis, spending, and estimated savings outcomes. It does not establish individual cure completion, equal access, household financial effects, long-run eradication, or national transferability.
